caption: Being away four days a week makes 'cooking at home' an expensive joke. Is R52 000 enough to justify the hours?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R52 000
p/m salary
Living in Krugersdorp
slides.body:
Male, 29
Single, no kids
Job: First officer, regional airline, based at Lanseria
Net salary: R52 000 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: 2 bed near Lanseria, short commute for early check-ins
slides.body: I picked the suburb for the drive time, not the suburb. I've seen it in daylight maybe six times.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.includes: Needed for 4am airport runs, no Uber does those reliably
slides.body: I did the maths on a cheaper car. The maths didn't account for missing a flight.

slides.title: Retirement annuity & TFSA
slides.body: Pilots don't get a company pension the way people assume. This is the whole plan.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Whatever's still good after a four-day roster away
slides.body: I've thrown out more expired milk than most people buy in a year.

slides.title: Medical certs & training renewals
slides.includes: Annual medical, sim checks, licence renewals
slides.body: This one's not optional. No current medical, no flying, no salary.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Medical aid, insurance, phone & fibre, eating out, subscriptions, savings, gym
slides.body: The roster makes routine expensive. Eating out isn't a treat when you're never home to cook.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R52 000. Better than most months, mostly because I was away and couldn't spend it.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded a few months of statements to Beyond Horizon to see what an irregular roster actually does to spending. Eating out was the answer.

No bank login needed.
